title: Depth Improves Training-Time Scaling for Difficult Tasks in Deep Linear Networks
abstract: arXiv:2610.35514v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Neural scaling laws describe the predictable power-law dependence of model performance on training time, dataset size, and model scale, with the exponents quantifying how performance changes with resources. Recent theory has shown how scaling exponents are shaped by the data distribution and the structure of the learning task, but whether network depth can improve training-time scaling has remained unsettled. Through a refined analysis of deep linear networks, we clarify that the task spectrum determines when increasing network depth improves training-time scaling. For spectrally difficult tasks, increasing depth improves the asymptotic training-time scaling exponent, whereas for easy tasks, the exponent remains independent of depth, with depth affecting only a logarithmic correction at the boundary between these regimes. translated_abstract: 神经缩放定律描述了模型性能对训练时间、数据集大小和模型规模的的可预测幂律依赖关系，其中的指数量化了性能随资源变化的程度。近期的理论研究表明，缩放指数由数据分布和学习任务的结构共同塑造，但网络深度能否改善训练时间缩放一直悬而未决。通过对深度线性网络的精细化分析，我们阐明了任务谱决定了何时增加网络深度能够改善训练时间缩放。对于谱上困难（spectrally difficult）的任务，增加深度可改善渐近的训练时间缩放指数；而对于简单任务，该指数与深度无关，深度仅在两种机制的边界处影响一个对数修正项。值得注意的是，我们发现一种由预测器范数主导的时间重参数化为……（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 本文通过对深度线性网络的分析证明，任务谱决定了深度何时有益：对于谱上困难的任务，增加网络深度能够改善训练时间缩放指数，而对于简单任务该指数与深度无关。
